 A British woman has drowned in the Bahamas after attempting to save her two children, who were swept away while snorkelling.
 The 36-year-old, who has not been named, died on Tuesday after being pulled from the water.
 She was holidaying with her husband and two sons on the island of Bimini when she was swept away by a strong current, police said. The boys were rescued from the water.
 A spokesman for the Royal Bahamas Police Force said the family had been on a snorkelling expedition to the south of the island.
 The spokesman added: “Preliminary information indicates that the deceased was snorkelling with her husband and two sons near the southern point of the island when a strong current reportedly swept both children away.
 “In an attempt to rescue her sons, the woman was also swept away. She was later rescued and transported to the ferry dock, where CPR was reportedly administered.
 “Officers responded and, upon arrival, learned that the woman had been transported to the local clinic for medical attention, where she was subsequently pronounced dead by a local doctor despite efforts to save her life.”
 The force said foul play was “not suspected”.
 Linty Stuart, the owner of L&A Water Taxi, told the Bahamian broadcaster ZNS that he captained the boat that pulled the family from the water.
 The family had been visiting the island on a cruise ship, according to ZNS.
 At least four people have drowned in waters off Bimini in the last two years, including two snorkellers.
 A spokesman for the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office said: “Our thoughts are with the family of a British woman who has died in the Bahamas.
 “We are in contact with the local authorities and providing support to her family.”
